title: Catholic vs private faith-certainty: public revelation versus private disclosure
source_text: VI. Praeterea Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae hic distinguunt certitudinem fidei in certitudinem fidei Catholicae, qua creduntur ea quae per Ecclesiae doctrinam & testimonium omnibus constare debent a Deo esse revelata; & in certitudinem fidei privatae, qua creduntur ea quae privatae alicui personae, non vero toti Ecclesiae a Deo revelata sunt; aut saltem quod ad commune fidei objectum non pertinent.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the doctors of the Roman Church here distinguish the certainty of faith into the certainty of Catholic faith, by which those things are believed which through the Church’s doctrine and testimony ought to be clear to all as revealed by God; and into the certainty of private faith, by which those things are believed which have been revealed by God to some private person, not to the whole Church, or at least do not belong to the common object of faith.
pass_b_english: Romans split faith-certainty into Catholic (public Church revelation) and private (personal revelation).
Only the former binds all as the common object of faith.
